output.reason: Recurring seasonal sneezing, itchy eyes and nasal stuffiness without reported fever, breathing difficulty or unilateral/bloody symptoms can be managed with over-the-counter measures and guidance alone.
output.patientMessage: You can start over-the-counter care today: a non-sedating antihistamine such as cetirizine or loratadine, plus a steroid nasal spray like fluticasone (takes 1-2 weeks for full benefit) and saline rinses. Your pattern fits typical pollen allergy. Limit decongestant sprays to 3 days. If you develop wheeze, trouble breathing, throat or tongue swelling, or hives, call 911. Fever, one-sided blockage, bloody discharge, or no improvement after 2 weeks — message a clinician here.
differential: Seasonal allergic rhinitis with allergic conjunctivitis

redFlags.concern: Breathing difficulty, wheeze or throat swelling

output.vitalSigns: No vital signs reported; whether any were measured is unknown.

citations.claim: Non-sedating second-generation antihistamines (cetirizine, loratadine) are preferred for ongoing daily allergy symptom control.
citations.limitation: ED reference synthesis; individual suitability not assessed.
